A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices A–D are readable, and relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original ROC-fairness and continual-learning experiments in Figures 1–8, plus empirical Jacobian singular values in Appendix A.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and numerical analyses, including the appendix results.

M1.justification: The hinge penalty, MSVR recursions and compositional update equations are retained. However, v2 Algorithm 2 line 15 adds a second objective-gradient assignment using the non-compositional estimator, conflicting with line 9 and Equation 27. The PDFs do not resolve whether this represents a procedural change or a transcription error.

E1.justification: Both versions use Adult, COMPAS and CheXpert for ROC fairness, and BDD100K with LAION400M samples for continual learning targeting foggy, overcast and tunnel classes. Appendix task exclusions are also unchanged.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparators remain the squared-hinge method and, for Adult and COMPAS, ICPPAC. Liu and Xu's addition to Table 1 is a theoretical literature comparison, not an added experimental baseline.

E3.justification: The reported models, sampling, metrics, penalty sweeps, learning-rate schedules and training budgets are retained. Both versions specify 60 epochs, batch sizes of 128 for fairness and 256 for continual learning, and 400 iterations per continual-learning epoch.

E4.justification: The penalty-parameter sensitivity curves and Appendix A's checks of Jacobian singular values are retained. New discussion of estimator fluctuations and regularity assumptions does not introduce additional empirical analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions report five-seed averaging and retain the same plotted variability bands. No empirical uncertainty procedure or statistical test is added; the new high-probability KKT statement concerns theory.

E6.justification: Appendix A newly reports approximately four hours per seed for the fairness experiments and twelve hours for continual learning, with comparable runtimes across methods. Performance and constraint curves in Figures 1–8 and all singular values in Table 2 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Lemmas 4.3–4.4 extend the sufficient conditions from differentiable constraints to subdifferentials and sub-Jacobians, with revised Appendix B proofs and singular-value terminology. New Corollary 5.4 and its Appendix C argument distinguish expected stationarity from high-probability feasibility and complementarity. The existing compositional convergence theorems are relocated to Appendix D, not newly introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: single-loop hinge-penalty algorithms, constant penalty parameters, O(epsilon^-6) complexity, compositional objectives, and validation on fairness and continual learning.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands applicability and limitation discussions: possible localization of the regularity condition, requirements for slack-variable reformulations, control of MSVR estimation fluctuations, and the slower rate relative to smooth equality-constrained optimization. It also discusses primal–dual extensions as future work.

D1.justification: Appendix A adds per-seed runtimes and specifies that continual learning uses two A100 40GB GPUs; v1 described the computing platform's node capacity instead. These are resource disclosures, without evidence that the experiments were rerun under changed settings.

R1.justification: v2 adds smoothing and primal–dual references, expands comparisons with slack-variable approaches, and removes the earlier self-citation. It adds the already-cited Liu and Xu work to Table 1 and refines the distinction to sampling constraints versus accessing all constraints, while acknowledging matching complexity.

P1.justification: Most prose and the overall section sequence are retained. Targeted restructuring moves Setting II from Section 5.2 into Appendix D and the Moreau-envelope lemma into Appendix B. Explanations and remarks expand, citations switch to author–year style, and acknowledgments and a concluding discussion are added.

P2.justification: The document adopts a substantially different journal layout, including the title and author block, typography, headers, text width, and figure sizing and placement. Algorithms now display formulas directly, and Table 1 gains a row. Figures 5–6 correct their captions from five constraints to four; the plotted results themselves are retained.

improvement.justification: The revised sufficient conditions, explicit stochastic interpretation of the KKT guarantee, expanded limitations and resource disclosures make the paper easier to assess. The conflicting gradient assignment introduced in Algorithm 2 partly offsets these gains. Overall, the revision provides a limited improvement in precision and transparency while retaining the empirical evidence.
